items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: He ended up teaching a course on Bill Evans that was very popular and really, really good.

ctx.x: Well yeah but that was quite a while ago. Thirty years probably you know. But I know it was figured out with mainly the three of us: Ray Wright, Bill Dobbins, and myself. Now those two guys were full time on the jazz side of things. I was teaching, you know, one- on-one saxophone lessons and clarinet to begin with and teaching ten hours of jazz which was an improvisation course and direct a band, that kind of thing. Probably a couple of courses, improv courses. So Ray and Bill mainly put it together with my…

know and then there was a couple of, at least one, musicologist — he was theory. But he was a pianist, an old jazz piano player that had done it. So he was really on top of it. He ended up teaching a course on Bill Evans that was very popular and really, really good. You know.

I wish I could remember who said this to me but they pointed out that today’s jazz major, instrumentalist, is much more likely to be able to step into a symphony gig and fill a part, rather than the other way around. That an orchestral musician would have much more trouble going playing Thad Jones/Mel Lewis charts.
